Skin tear management (AJGP Table 1):
INCORRECT dressing choice — adhesive bordered foam can cause further skin tears on fragile skin. Correct approach:

Primary dressing: Apply SILICONE-COATED foam dressing directly over the wound.
  — Reposition the skin flap before applying the dressing.
  — Do NOT use any ADHESIVE products on fragile skin — they may contribute to further skin tears, especially on forearms and hands of the elderly.
  — Non-silicone foam types should be avoided in patients with fragile skin.

Barrier wipe: Use a barrier wipe UNDER the foam to secure application, reduce maceration, and protect the skin on removal.

Removal: Use remover wipes when removing the dressing from fragile skin. Remove in a direction that does NOT disturb viable tissue edges and flaps.

If bleeding: Apply haemostatic alginate dressing as PRIMARY under the silicone foam.

NPWT is NOT appropriate as sole treatment in this wound, for two reasons:

1. NPWT IS CONTRAINDICATED in necrotic wound bed or eschar — the necrotic tissue acts as a barrier to new tissue growth. This wound has 50% necrotic tissue.
2. NPWT is an ADJUNCT treatment only. It does not replace surgical procedures and is not a panacea. It prepares the wound bed for a greater chance of successful closure.

Additional NPWT contraindications:
  — Untreated infection (deep extension of infectious focus)
  — Clotting disorders (risk of bleeding)
  — Neoplastic tissue in wound area

Correct approach for this wound (Type 8 — wet, infected, >25% necrotic):
First: Surgical/mechanical debridement (strongly recommended).
Interim dressing: Alginate, Silver dressing, Hydrofibre, Foam, Charcoal, Polymeric membrane, or Iodine-based dressing.
Antibiotic: Yes, based on C&S.
NPWT may be considered AFTER adequate debridement.

For very heavy exudate where foam alone saturates within 24 hours, consider these alternatives or combinations (Wound Type 2 — clean wet wound):

1. ALGINATE (primary dressing):
   — Absorbs up to 20 times its own weight — highest absorption capacity
   — Forms a gel on contact with wound fluid that absorbs and contains exudate
   — Promotes healing by maintaining physiologically moist environment
   — Available in sheets or rope form; can fill cavities
   — Always needs a secondary dressing over it
   — Frequency: 2–5 days
   — Note: residue must be washed off during cleansing

2. HYDROFIBRE (primary dressing):
   — Manages heavy exuding wounds
   — Creates soft cohesive gel that conforms to wound surface
   — Comfortable and non-traumatic on removal
   — Reduces risk of maceration
   — Needs secondary dressing
   — Frequency: 2–5 days

3. FOAM (secondary or alone):
   — Highly absorbent but less so than alginate for very heavy exudate
   — Frequency: 2–3 days

For macerated periwound skin: apply skin protection/barrier before dressing.
